title: bug: postflight-worktree.cjs wt-resume pins neither half of the L2 marker-scan union, so three sh mutants of the completion's conflict check survive
description:
Problem: at a worktree completion, L2's marker check scans the union of `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` (unmerged paths) and `task.landingRetry.paths`. It scans whenever landingRetry is set, not only while MERGE_HEAD exists, and a marker left is MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT. The wt-resume chain in scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs has exactly one conflict path, src/a.txt, which is both a retry path and unmerged. So no case pins either half of the union, or the trigger, on its own.

Evidence: QA comment-cf8ade2050f840a3bb2d6b15b0a05787 on task-b1ca54f2 (WT-19), from the WT-11 review (task-dd1ee586, approved at 7cd8e423). Three sh mutants survived the wt-resume case: (1) dropping the `--diff-filter=U` half of the union; (2) dropping the landingRetry.paths half; (3) scanning only while MERGE_HEAD exists. The mutant driver is D:\moe-scratch\qa-wt11\mut\run.sh, with details in Serena memory decision-worktree-pending-merge-checkpoint. The production code for all three is present and correct by inspection, so this is a test gap, not a wrapper defect.

Impact: a later edit that drops either half, or narrows the trigger, passes the suite. A completion could then land conflict markers on the target: markers left on a path outside landingRetry.paths, or a retry path's markers after `merge --quit` has removed MERGE_HEAD.

Fix: add two cases to postflight-worktree.cjs and run each in both engines (sh and ps1):
(a) a resume whose merge conflicts on a path outside landingRetry.paths; a completion that leaves markers there prints MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT, lands nothing and routes conflict;
(b) markers left in a landingRetry path with no MERGE_HEAD; the completion also refuses.
Prove each case kills its mutant: temporarily apply the mutant, see the case fail, then restore. Test files only; no wrapper change unless a case exposes a real defect, which then gets its own row.
definitionOfDone: postflight-worktree.cjs has case (a): a conflict on a path outside landingRetry.paths, with markers left at completion, gives MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT, nothing lands, and the route is conflict, on both the sh and ps1 engines
postflight-worktree.cjs has case (b): markers in a landingRetry path with no MERGE_HEAD refuse the completion the same way, on both engines
Each of the three mutants named in the description fails at least one new case (record the RED runs), and the restored wrapper passes
node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash and postflight-safe.mjs powershell (Windows node) pass, with counts recorded; bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes
No assertion in an existing case is weakened, and scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} are unchanged

implementationPlan.note: Added wtResumeUnmerged directly after wtResume and registered 'wt-resume-unmerged' right after 'wt-resume' in the case table. A gate-routed unlanded completion (retry paths [], 1 gate run) is the premise check. The resume then conflicts on src/a.txt against main B. The completion asserts: LANDING-CONFLICT prompt, main==B, MERGE_HEAD==B, markers in W, the [WARN] MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT line, one unlanded/conflict/['src/a.txt'] finalize, stored retry paths ['src/a.txt'], and no new gate run. sh run on the unmodified wrapper: `[worktree] wt-resume-unmerged ok` (1 ok, 0 failed, 1m22s).

implementationPlan.description:
Case (b): the landingRetry.paths half and the retry-only trigger. Same file, Edit tool. Place `async function wtResumeRetryPath()` right after wtResumeUnmerged, and register it right after 'wt-resume-unmerged' in the case table.

Head comment (2-3 lines): markers stay in a retry path after the pending merge was committed by hand, so MERGE_HEAD is gone, nothing is unmerged and the resume's merge is a no-op. Only the retry paths, scanned because landingRetry is set, can catch them.

Steps:
- p = repo('wt-resume-retry-path', {settings: LANDS}). mh = () => revOf(p.W, 'MERGE_HEAD').
- landRun(p, 'wt-resume-retry-path-0', {'src/a.txt': 'task a\n'}).
- b = commitOn(p, 'refs/heads/main', {'src/a.txt': 'main a\n'}).
- landRun(p, 'wt-resume-retry-path-1', {}, REVIEW): merge-tree conflict, unlanded 'conflict' with paths ['src/a.txt'].
- landRun(p, 'wt-resume-retry-path-2', {}): the resume (WORKING) merges main, leaving markers and MERGE_HEAD; its checkpoint keeps both (see the wt-resume chain).
- Commit that merge outside the wrapper: git(p.W, 'add', '--', 'src/a.txt'); git(p.W, 'commit', '-q', '--no-verify', '--no-edit'). This stands in for any tip that carries markers with no pending merge, such as a human commit or an older wrapper.
- Assert, so the case is non-vacuous: mh() === null; the markers are in W/src/a.txt; git(p.W, 'ls-files', '-u') === ''; deepEqual(retryOf(p).paths, ['src/a.txt']); W's HEAD has b as an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`).
- main0 = mainOf(p) (=== b).
- r = landRun(p, 'wt-resume-retry-path-3', {}, {...REVIEW, WT_CLI_RECORD: rec}, {type: 'claude'}).
- One assert.deepEqual with tail(r.log). It expects:
  - promptOf(rec) === 'LANDING-RETRY: conflict', which proves no merge was pending and nothing was unmerged at the completion;
  - mainOf(p) === main0;
  - mh() === null;
  - r.log includes '[WARN] MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT';
  - the last unlanded(p) entry is ['unlanded', 'conflict', ['src/a.txt']];
  - no new 'landed' entry in finals(p).

Both new cases must run unchanged under the sh engine (postflight.sh) and the ps1 engines (postflight.ps1): use only the suite's git and fs helpers, never a shell-specific command. Do not touch any existing case or assertion. scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} stay unchanged.
implementationPlan.note: Added wtResumeRetryPath right after wtResumeUnmerged, and registered 'wt-resume-retry-path' right after 'wt-resume-unmerged'. The chain: checkpoint T, main B changes src/a.txt, a REVIEW run conflict-routes with retry paths ['src/a.txt'] (asserted), and the WORKING resume leaves markers + MERGE_HEAD==B (asserted). The merge is then committed by hand in W (add + commit --no-verify --no-edit). Non-vacuity check: no MERGE_HEAD, markers kept, ls-files -u empty, retry paths ['src/a.txt'], B an ancestor of W HEAD, main==B. Completion: LANDING-RETRY: conflict prompt, main unmoved, no MERGE_HEAD, markers kept, [WARN] MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT, one unlanded/conflict/['src/a.txt'] finalize, no landed finalize. Runs on the unmodified wrappers: sh `[worktree] wt-resume-retry-path ok` (1 ok, 0 failed); PS 5.1 `[worktree] wt-resume-unmerged ok`, `[worktree] wt-resume-retry-path ok` (2 ok, 0 failed, 48s).

implementationPlan.description:
Mutant RED proofs (DoD 3, run in scratch only, per mem:gotcha-postflight-worktree-mutant-copy). For each run, copy this worktree's whole scripts/ tree (it holds the new uncommitted cases) into its own dir under /mnt/d/moe-scratch/c6436215-mut/<name>/. Put a private copy of postflight-fake-proxy.js in <dir>/tmp. Apply one fixed-string swap with a needle count of exactly 1; keep the ps1 BOM by using byte-level read and write. Never edit the worktree's wrapper.

First, an unmutated control on each engine: both new cases plus wt-resume are ok.
- sh: `env -u MOE_SESSION_ID -u MOE_ATTEMPT_ID -u MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-resume-unmerged,wt-resume-retry-path node <copy>/scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs sh <copy>/scripts/moe-agent.sh <dir>/tmp/fake-proxy.js <dir>/tmp $(command -v bash)`.
- ps1: `cd /mnt/d/... && MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=... WSLENV=MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY "/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" '<D:\copy>\scripts\tests\postflight-worktree.cjs' ps1 '<D:\copy>\scripts\moe-agent.ps1' '<D:\dir>\tmp\fake-proxy.js' '<D:\dir>\tmp' powershell`.

sh mutants, the three the description names; each must give an AssertionError on its case:
- M1: `cat "${MOE_WT_RETRY_PATHS:-/dev/null}" 2>/dev/null; git -C "$1" diff --name-only -z --diff-filter=U 2>/dev/null)` becomes `cat "${MOE_WT_RETRY_PATHS:-/dev/null}" 2>/dev/null)`. wt-resume-unmerged must fail.
- M2: `< <(cat "${MOE_WT_RETRY_PATHS:-/dev/null}" 2>/dev/null; git -C "$1"` becomes `< <(git -C "$1"`. wt-resume-retry-path must fail.
- M3: `[ -n "$mh" ] || [ -n "${MOE_WT_RETRY:-}" ] || return 0` becomes `[ -n "$mh" ] || return 0`. wt-resume-retry-path must fail.

ps1 twins, so the cases bite on both engines:
- P1: `(@($script:MoeWtRetryPaths) + @(Get-MoeUnmergedPaths $WorktreePath))` becomes `(@($script:MoeWtRetryPaths))`.
- P2: the same expression becomes `(@(Get-MoeUnmergedPaths $WorktreePath))`.
- P3: `if ($Internal -and ($mh -or $script:MoeWtRetry)) {` becomes `if ($Internal -and $mh) {`.
The expected kills mirror M1-M3.

A mutant that fails with anything other than an AssertionError on its target case (a harness TypeError, a timeout) is not a kill: fix the copy and re-run. Record each result line ('[worktree] <case> FAILED: AssertionError: ...') for the completion summary. When the review is done, delete the scratch copies you made, and only those.

Verification test gate, once, fresh, from the task worktree after the last tracked edit. Its output is the complete_task evidence. Run exactly (about 70+ min: run it as one background job, wait for its exit, then paste the tail):

- The sh targeted run prints `[worktree] 4 ok, 0 failed` and the ps1 targeted run `[worktree] 3 ok, 0 failed`. These are the DoD 4 counts.
- Both postflight-safe lines are `{"engine":...,"exit":0,...,"failureClass":"NONE",...}`.

A second targeted run uses the same $S parent, so wait for the first to finish. Delete $S afterwards. Kill only PIDs you started yourself, never by pattern.

Adversarial self-review of this test-only diff (adversarial-self-review skill).

Check:
- `git diff` shows changes to scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs only, and scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} are byte-identical to the target.
- No existing case, helper or assertion changed: only the two new functions and two new table entries. The new code sits beside wt-resume, not at the end of the file or of the table.

Two new postflight-worktree.cjs cases, run by both engines, pin each half of the L2 marker-scan union and its landingRetry trigger.
- wt-resume-unmerged: after a gate-routed unlanded completion (retry paths []), main changes src/a.txt. The resume's merge conflicts, and a completion that keeps the markers is refused with MOE_WORKTREE_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT, lands nothing and routes 'conflict'.
- wt-resume-retry-path: markers stay in retry path src/a.txt after the pending merge was committed by hand, so there is no MERGE_HEAD and nothing unmerged. The completion is still refused the same way.
No wrapper change.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Case (a) could reuse a 'conflict' route with a second conflicting path, but a non-conflict route (gate, which stores paths []) puts the resume's conflict outside landingRetry.paths by construction, so M1 cannot hide behind a retry path. The 'contention' route also works (WT_GIT_FAIL:'-m'), but its replay knobs add noise.

Case (b) needs markers in a retry path with no MERGE_HEAD. Running `merge --quit` by hand fails: the next pre-flight's worktree_resume would merge again over a dirty index and stop with MOE_WORKTREE_RESUME_FAILED. Committing the pending merge by hand instead makes W clean with B as an ancestor, so worktree_resume's `merge --no-commit --no-ff` is 'Already up to date' (exit 0, no MERGE_HEAD, no unmerged paths), and the completion's L2 is then triggered by landingRetry alone.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- sh wt_merge_check (moe-agent.sh :7092-7111): it returns early unless MERGE_HEAD or MOE_WT_RETRY is set, then scans `cat $MOE_WT_RETRY_PATHS; git diff --name-only -z --diff-filter=U`.
- ps1 twin (:6634-6642): `if ($Internal -and ($mh -or $script:MoeWtRetry))`, scanning `@($script:MoeWtRetryPaths) + @(Get-MoeUnmergedPaths ...)`.
- worktree_resume (:7793+) reloads landingRetry from the pre-flight get_context. It reuses an existing MERGE_HEAD, and otherwise merges the target with hooks off.
- The fake proxy (:150-155, :597-599) stores {reason, paths: conflictPaths||[], ...} on an unlanded finalize, serves it as task.landingRetry, and clears it on landed.
- MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY selects cases. Only a typed CLI ({type:'claude'}) forwards the prompt argv to WT_CLI_RECORD.
planningNotes.risks:
(a) The ps1 engine runs the same JS cases, so avoid any POSIX-only call; the suite's git() is cross-platform.
(b) Timings: sh resume cases take 1-3 min each and PS 5.1 about 4 min. The full gates take about 25 min for bash and about 45 min for PS 5.1, so run them in the background.
(c) A harness TypeError is not a mutant kill. Copy the whole scripts/ tree per mutant and run a control first.
(d) Windows node through WSL interop eats a loop's stdin: give each iteration < /dev/null.
(e) Keep the placement beside wt-resume (governor) so that task-e3e81c45's cases merge cleanly; a residual conflict takes the conflict-resume path.
